newsitem.title: FRANCE: Lyonnaise rules out immediate Suez merger.
newsitem.headline: Lyonnaise rules out immediate Suez merger.

text.p: Lyonnaise des Eaux chairman Jerome Monod said on Thursday he was satisfied with the capital structure of the group, ruling out a near-term merger with Compagnie de Suez.
"We have a diversified shareholding and we are keen on that. We agreed that it was the best configuration possible," he told a news conference on Thursday.
Suez holds 18 percent of the French utilities company's capital and has "a little more than 20 percent" of the voting rights, he said.
Asked whether he would absolutely rule out a merger with Suez, Monod said "In life, you must never rule out anything."
But he said it was at the moment in the company's interest to keep its current structure and to develop without raising capital.

Rumours of a merger between the two groups resurfaced on September 17 when a Suez subsidiary, Societe Generale de Belgique, said it had bought a 24.47 percent stake in Tractebel from rival Belgian holding company Groupe Bruxelles Lambert.
